difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma, six assertions: for a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the sheaf K_X is the sum and the product over generic points of the pushforwards of the residue fields, it is a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras, the sheaf of meromorphic sections of any quasi-coherent F is quasi-coherent, the stalk S_x is the set of nonzerodivisors, K_{X,x} is the total quotient ring, K_X(U) is the total quotient ring of O_X(U) for affine U, and the ring of rational functions is the ring of global meromorphic functions (source lines 6424-6456). The proof records the lemma as the special case of the general weakly-associated statement, the reason being that on a reduced scheme the weakly associated points are exactly the generic points.
